parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs criminalisation of same-sex conduct with no legal gender recognition, so an outed trans visitor is legally their birth sex and any relationship can fall inside Article 629. Documented state-tolerated targeting is severe: 2023 venue raids, a municipal call for public reporting, warrantless police searches, physical abuse in detention, and police disclosure of detainees' orientation to family (one suicide). Custody placement by birth sex is documented (a trans woman held a year in a men's prison, abused). No hate-crime cover, no registration for LGBTI groups, no remedies that work; outed people risk violence and ostracism. No execution pathway is documented, keeping this above the extreme floor.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; trans visitors' documents carry birth sex. Mismatch invites scrutiny; documented extortion attempt after passport discovery led to reporting, detention and a year in a men's prison.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Dossier records no border tolerance, X-marker acceptance or document-mismatch guidance.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discovery → extortion/reporting → criminal-law framing under Article 629 → birth-sex custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Warrantless residential searches after neighbour complaints; physical abuse during detention; denial of counsel and inmate assault (2014); trans woman held ~1 year in a men's prison with staff and inmate abuse; police disclosed detainees' orientation to family.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Enforcement of Article 629 is described as rare, but crackdowns (Aug 2023) and abuse records offset that.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing or reporting triggers detention where birth-sex placement and abusive custody apply with no effective remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Capital's Peace and Security Administration Bureau directed measures against venues and urged public reporting; 2023 raids on guest houses and hotels — state actors targeting perceived LGBTIQ presence in visitor-facing lodging.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No subnational protective regime appears; record is capital-only with no regional contrast.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Lodging exposure meets the criminalisation framework: hotel/guest-house suspicion can escalate to arrest.

care_services.exposure: Stigma in healthcare documented; no pathway for legal sex change; HIV stigma affects services; AIDS centre callers sought behaviour change to avoid discrimination.
care_services.interaction: A trans visitor needing care risks disclosure to staff in a society where outing brings violence and ostracism.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State and non-state threat-framing: Aug 2023 security crackdown, official reporting call, online incitement urging stabbing/killing ending in physical attacks, religious campaigns for harsher penalties, media constructing homophobia.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. A proposed non-pardonable-offence bill was cancelled, a limited positive.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses public hostility and reduces any expectation of police protection for an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented specifically. A child accompanying an outed adult inherits the same criminalisation, violence and outing risks; anti-LGBTIQ incitement references children as victims, raising family/parent exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent's outing extends to household; no custody or child-protection safeguards for gender-diverse families appear.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Outing risks physical violence and ostracism; 2023 incitement wave produced physical attacks; no hate-crime or hate-speech law covering gender identity; lack of police protection documented; harassment rising through end-2023.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No evidence prosecutions of attackers follow.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal violence plus absent state protection means an outed visitor has no realistic remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: LGBTI groups cannot register; no hate-crime cover; no freedom from arbitrary arrest on gender-identity grounds; civic-space restrictions; activists report surveillance and entrapment; near-total concealment of identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Only that enforcement of Article 629 is rare and a 2014 escalation bill was cancelled; barometer shows a stable (not worsening) picture 2011–2024.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absent remedies, documented abuse recurs; oversight findings do not change practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: Varnalia has routine arrest, months of pretrial custody and a latent capital clause. Here custody abuse and birth-sex prison placement are documented, but Article 629 enforcement is described as rare and no capital provision touches gender presentation, so slightly above 0.15.

Higher than this anchor: Ostravia's worst feature is birth-sex prison placement plus a cross-dressing statute with slow remedies. The dossier here adds state venue raids, warrantless searches, police disclosure of identity, incitement-driven attacks and no recourse at all — a heavier state-tolerated targeting tier.

Far higher: Kestrel Isles' exposure is administrative secondary screening and discretionary refusal with appeal desks and consular notification. The dossier here documents criminal-law exposure, abusive custody and societal violence — several precedence tiers below it.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is cumulative: no legal gender recognition means the visitor's documents and legal sex never match their lived gender, feeding directly into a criminal same-sex-conduct statute that state actors invoked in 2023 venue raids and a public reporting campaign. Outing therefore reaches border, lodging, custody and street simultaneously. Documented custody abuse, police disclosure of identity to family, warrantless searches, and incitement-driven attacks occur with no hate-crime cover, no registrable advocacy and no working remedy. Enforcement of the statute is rare and no execution pathway is documented, which lifts the rating above the 0.15 tier; but state-tolerated targeting plus birth-sex custody with no recourse places it firmly in the 0.15–0.22 range for both solitary adults and adults travelling with a minor.
